title: Clean energy
blocks_why: Most of this is private investment, which follows prices and policy as much as available money.
need_text: Around $4.5 trillion a year by the early 2030s on the IEA's net-zero path
covers: All clean energy investment worldwide, public and private: renewables, nuclear, grids, storage, efficiency and electrification.
note: The 2026 figure is the IEA's estimate for this year. The need comes from one scenario, published in 2023.

title: Childhood vaccination
blocks_why: Gavi's board cut its working budget to $10 billion after the pledges fell short of its target.
spent_source: Gavi, resource mobilisation update to the Board, July 2026
need_text: $11.9 billion for 2026 to 2030, Gavi's own target
covers: Gavi only: donor money for vaccines in lower-income countries over five years. Not all vaccination spending.
outcome: At full funding, Gavi aims to protect 500 million children and avert 8 to 9 million future deaths.
note: Figures are five-year totals, not yearly.

title: Hunger
blocks_why: The models cost safety nets, farm support and rural development; they assume the money is spent on what works.
need_text: An extra $33 billion a year (Ceres2030) to $39 to $50 billion a year (ZEF and FAO), on top of current spending
covers: Extra public spending to 2030 from donors and from lower-income countries' own budgets. Ceres2030 says donors already spend about $12 billion a year.
outcome: Ceres2030 models the extra $33 billion keeping 490 million people out of hunger, against 660 million people hungry in 2030 without it.
note: Both estimates were made in 2020 and 2021, before the recent rise in food prices. They are shown as a range, not averaged.

title: Nature
blocks_why: UNEP finds $7.3 trillion a year flowing into activities that harm nature, against $220 billion for it.
spent_text: $220 billion in 2023, about 90% of it public
spent_source: UNEP, State of Finance for Nature 2026, via IISD SDG Knowledge Hub
need_text: $571 billion a year by 2030 to meet the biodiversity, climate and land-restoration targets
need_source: UNEP, State of Finance for Nature 2026
covers: "Nature-based solutions": protecting and restoring ecosystems, including forests and farming for climate. Wider than wildlife protection alone.
note: UNEP's own page could not be opened from here; the figures were read from the IISD summary of the report.

title: Asteroid detection
blocks_why: The constraint is building and launching the NEO Surveyor telescope, due by June 2028.
spent_text: $300 million for NEO Surveyor in US fiscal year 2026
spent_source: The Planetary Society, enacted FY2026 NASA budget
covers: US government spending only. NEO Surveyor's total cost estimate is $1.6 billion.
outcome: NASA's Inspector General found budget projections show a significant drop in planetary defense funding after fiscal 2027.
outcome_source: NASA Office of Inspector General, June 2025
note: The mission is funded within its $1.6 billion baseline, so there is no gap to show.
